questions.question: Why can an endpoint returning successful responses still be an unhealthy ML product?
options: Successful responses prove only that labels have arrived
Data, model quality, or cohort harm can regress while serving remains available
HTTP status automatically measures calibration
A deployed model cannot change its input distribution
questions.explanation: Serving health is one plane. Data validity, model behavior, and product outcomes can fail independently.

questions.question: Which event fields best support prediction traceability?
options: Only the model's display name
A dashboard URL and current CPU usage
Prediction ID, event time, model and feature versions, decision, and outcome join key
A raw copy of every private feature without retention limits
questions.explanation: The trace needs stable lineage and join fields while respecting privacy and retention controls.

questions.question: A cohort has 250 predictions, but only 200 outcomes have arrived. What label coverage should the monitor report?
questions.explanation: Label coverage is joined outcomes divided by predictions: 200 / 250 = 0.80, or 80%.

questions.question: The decision log fails while inference responses continue. What is the correct interpretation?
options: The system is healthy because latency is unchanged
All missing events should be counted as incorrect predictions
The model should retrain immediately
Serving is available, but the ML product is blind and rollout risk should be contained
questions.explanation: Telemetry loss breaks evidence and outcome joins even when the online path still serves requests.

questions.question: A feature distribution changes, but mature quality and product guardrails remain healthy. What should happen first?
options: Investigate the change and keep watching impact before choosing mitigation
Promote an automatically retrained model
Page every operator regardless of persistence or sample size
Delete the reference distribution
questions.explanation: Drift is evidence of change, not proof of harm. Confirm persistence, scope, and consequence before acting.

questions.question: Which alert is actionable?
options: A graph changed sometime today
Accuracy is different
High-risk false negatives breached the release guardrail; page the named owner and run the rollback procedure
A statistical test returned a small p-value
questions.explanation: An actionable alert identifies impact, severity, ownership, and a safe response tied to the failure mode.
